questions.text: Let G = (V, E) be a simple undirected graph, and s be a particular vertex in it called the source. For [latex]x \in V[/latex], let d(x) denote the shortest distance in G from s to x. A breadth first search (BFS) is performed starting at s. Let T be the resultant BFS tree. If (u,v) is an edge of G that is not in T, then which one of the following CANNOT be the value of d(u)-d(v)?
questions.solution:
In BFS of an undirected graph, every edge joins vertices whose levels differ by at most 1. If d(u) [latex]-[/latex] d(v) were 2, v would have discovered u earlier, giving d(u) = d(v) + 1.

So d(u) [latex]-[/latex] d(v) can only be [latex]-[/latex]1, 0 or 1.

Answer: 2

questions.text: Which one of the following is the recurrence equation for the worst case time complexity of the Quicksort algorithm for sorting n ( [latex]\geq[/latex]2) numbers? In the recurrence equations given in the options below, c is a constant.
questions.solution:
Worst case: the pivot is the smallest/largest each time, so the partition sizes are n[latex]-[/latex]1 and 1, plus linear partitioning work.

T(n) = T(n [latex]-[/latex] 1) + T(1) + cn

Answer: T(n) = T(n-1) + T(1) + cn

Checking each statement:
- Prim's MST: greedy (ii)
- Floyd-Warshall: dynamic programming (iii)
- Mergesort: divide and conquer (iv)
- Hamiltonian circuit: backtracking (i)

Answer: P-ii, Q-iii, R-iv, S-i

questions.text:
Consider the following sorting algorithms.
I. Quicksort
II. Heapsort
III> Mergesort
Which of them perform in least time in the worst case?
questions.solution:
Worst case: Quicksort [latex]O(n^2)[/latex], Heapsort [latex]O(n\log n)[/latex], Mergesort [latex]O(n\log n)[/latex].

Answer: II and III only

Consider the decision problem 2CNFSAT defined as follows:
{ [latex]\phi[/latex] | [latex]\phi[/latex] is a satisfiable propositional formula in CNF with at most two literal per clause}
For example, [latex]\phi =(x_{1} \vee x_{2}) \wedge (x_{1} \vee \bar{x_{3}}) \wedge (x_{2} \vee x_{4})[/latex] is a Boolean formula and it is in 2CNFSAT.
The decision problem 2CNFSAT is
questions.solution:
Each clause [latex](a\vee b)[/latex] gives implications [latex] eg a ightarrow b[/latex] and [latex] eg b ightarrow a[/latex]. The formula is unsatisfiable iff some x reaches [latex] eg x[/latex] and [latex] eg x[/latex] reaches x in this implication graph.

So 2-SAT is solved in polynomial (linear) time by graph reachability.

Answer: solvable in polynomial time by reduction to directed graph reachability
